title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Morgan Moon appearance separates received sunlight from Earth-facing brightness
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. In the complete normalized 5r-C stanza of Morgan M.721, the Moon is said to have no light of its own; the Sun lights the part it sees; the visible figure varies; and the amount of light shown above Earth increases as the Moon is farther from the Sun and decreases as it approaches. The source distinguishes the body, the illuminated portion, and the Earth-facing appearance, rather than giving a complete labelled phase-day sequence. Preserve its stated relation without correcting it to modern orbital terminology, importing another witness's rubric, or inventing phase labels. The claim is a normalized working reading from a probably later-fifteenth-century codex, not a diplomatic transcription or independent early-fifteenth-century witness. The local source also has eclipse stanzas, phase-linked medical claims, diagrams with unresolved labels, and a gendered stereotype; this stanza cannot license silently flattening or dropping that surrounding material in any eventual whole-unit comparison. No target unit, forms, or meanings are assigned. Duplicate navigation returned IDEA000786 as a related same-source celestial light/body model, but this proposal's declared contrast isolates the farther/more versus nearer/less Earth-facing brightness relation; there is no exact declared-design match and this is not a novelty finding.

design.mechanism: A luminous source illuminates only an exposed portion of a non-self-luminous body; changing source-body separation is related in the source to changing Earth-facing brightness.
design.unit: The complete 5r-C stanza within the retained complete local reading of Morgan M.721 fols.5r–5v; no Voynich target unit selected.
design.contrast: Keep lunar body identity, received sunlight, illuminated portion, and observed brightness distinct; rival flattening assigns one body both the light source and the light-receiving role or substitutes a generic phase-name list for the written relation.
design.prediction: A future complete candidate must preserve the non-self-emission claim, Sun-to-exposed-part relation, and the stated farther/more versus nearer/less appearance relation, while leaving the source's uncertain wording and absent phase labels unresolved.
design.scope: Exploratory source-content hypothesis only; target meaning unbound, no target forms assigned, not a selected experiment.

source_evidence.quote:
Senza lume da sé ma tutta obscura
Quanta ne vede il sole tanto ne accende
Per questo è variabile sua figura
Perché tra su et giù mezza resplende
Et quanto è più distante sua misura
Dal sole tanto ogni dì più lume rende
Sopra la terra e quando si rappressa
Ogni dì scema suo lume da essa
